name: Workouts and fitness
summary: A good app helps you get through a specific workout: choose a plan you can do, log the sets, and pick up from that point next time.
lead:
A plan looks convincing until the person reaches the gym: the machine they need is taken, today’s weight is different, and the phone is awkward to hold. At home there are other circumstances — little time, a small screen and sessions that have to be interrupted.

So an app is worth looking at across the whole path of a session: understanding the conditions, recording what was done, saving the result and the place in the program. Some problems call for fixing the log, others point to a separate scenario — a home video workout, say, or a trainer working with a client. Not every missing button becomes a product of its own.

audiencesArt.alt: Different jobs in the “Workouts and fitness” category.

audiences.title: Following a strength program
audiences.body: A person arrives with a plan, looks at their previous sets and records what they did today. They need a recognizable order of exercises and a way to refine the values. The history should help them find their way around their own work without reconstructing it from memory again.

audiences.title: Training at home from a demonstration
audiences.body: You need to see the movements, hear the explanation and have time to move on to the next action. The phone or the big screen becomes part of the session. Pausing and coming back should keep its place, so the right moment doesn’t have to be found all over again.

audiences.title: Finding a format of sessions that suits
audiences.body: What matters for the choice is the specific movements, the body positions and the equipment available. A person wants to know the content in advance and to say what doesn’t suit them. A general label of age or level is no substitute for that information about a program.

sections.title: Arriving with a plan you can do
sections.intro: Choosing a program starts with today’s conditions: the time, the equipment and movements you understand.

observations.title: Seeing the previous weight and recording today’s
passages: A program can suggest the weight for the next session and let you change how fast it rises. Users value how convenient that continuation is, but their personal accounts of how they feel do not prove the calculation suits other people. The suggestion has to be shown separately from what has already been done.

The current entry needs context: what was done last time, what is planned today, and what actually came out. When those values are mixed together, it isn’t clear which part of the history an edit changes. The log has to allow today’s result to be saved without being fitted to the program’s expectations.

The chosen makeup of the sessions has to persist too. If an exercise that was added disappears the next day, the user has to explain the plan all over again. Before the next session it helps to show the changes and to keep access to the earlier version; this is a concrete job of preserving decisions, not a new AI coach feature.

quotes.text: Easy to follow the program when it auto-adjusts your weight to lift, and you can custom it to increase faster or slower as needed. I have had better sleep and my back pain has disappeared since I began lifting.

Interface is good. But the app itself is frustratingly dumb. It has no context for timing of workouts or its place in a series. For example, it gets confused when you previously did a 225x8 bench press set (first workout of the day) and can't seem to understand why you won't get the same weight afte

I like the idea of the AI coach but this one glitches a lot. It will add a new exercise to my routine and then a day later revert back to the previous routine that didn't have the exercise. It adds it again when I remind it.

placements.title: Seeing the previous weight and recording today’s

observations.title: Understanding how a trainer runs a program
passages: A ready-made program can remove the need to put a session together yourself. The review below values the confidence of walking into the gym: the person already knows what they will be working on. For a first look, it matters to show an ordinary session and where it sits in the series.

But a ready-made plan doesn’t do away with editing. If some of the supersets need to be turned off and there is no way to do it, the simplicity of the initial choice stops helping. Before the start it is worth showing which changes the interface allows and how they will be kept.

The manner of the guidance is another reason to come back. A familiar trainer’s voice can matter right in the middle of a movement. That benefit should be told apart from a specialist working personally with a client’s log: a catalog of recordings and a trainer’s workspace solve different problems, even when both use video.

quotes.text: I love, love, love this app (especially the women centered part). It has made me feel more confident in the gym and I go in knowing what I'm working on. I struggle with making my own workouts and routine and this completely erased that worry.

It's a straight forward app that is great when you can't think of what to do. HOWEVER, not being able to change/adjust is irritating. I want to turn some of the supersets off but can't. Also, it is clearly targeted for men given the weight suggestions or women who want to bulk. I find the weight rec

placements.title: Understanding how a trainer runs a program

observations.title: Knowing the conditions before the first movement
passages: An expectation of a chair session is at odds with a program that requires getting down on the floor. Suggesting again a movement that the person skips every time creates a similar problem: the app takes no account of a condition already stated. As a result part of the plan stays undoable for the scenario chosen.

The catalog has to show body positions, equipment and transitions in advance, and preferences have to persist for later choices. A skip and a swap both need to be reflected clearly in the plan. Where limitations are individual, what a program contains is agreed with a specialist; the interface’s job is to convey the conditions and the chosen changes accurately.

The “at home” filter is too broad: at home there may be nothing but a chair and ten free minutes. A more precise description lists the supports, the body positions and the equipment. And filtering by conditions does not confirm that a session is medically suitable: individual limitations call for a specialist’s decision, and the interface keeps and displays that decision.

quotes.text: The rest period between exercises isn't long enough to get into position for the next exercise. I am physically incapable of doing some of the exercises and skip them every workout, but they keep coming up in my workouts anyway, and I end up not getting a full workout because there's nothing to repl
My shoulder will not allow me to do push-ups.
No chair exercises for seniors. A lot of the 'senior' workouts included floor exercises. If I get down on the floor, I'm not able to get back up again LOL.

sections.title: Not being distracted from the session
sections.intro: Between sets the interface should ask for little attention. A watch, a video and a timer help only when they continue one and the same scenario.

observations.title: Logging a set from the wrist
passages: Marking a set from the wrist saves actions, as long as the watch and the phone show one and the same session. When they fall out of sync, instead of the next set the person is working out which device kept the result.

A brief loss of connection matters most. A mark made on the watch has to be saved locally and appear on the phone later without a duplicate. The user needs to see what has already been recorded and what is still waiting to be sent, with a way to correct a wrong value.

The watch also needs context for the next entry. With no previous weight and no rep count, the phone has to come out again. So testing the scenario covers not only tapping “Done”, but also looking at previous values, editing them, and finishing the whole workout.

quotes.text: When it's working properly, the app is great and the syncing with the Apple Watch makes staying on track at the gym so easy. Problem is when the two go out of sync, about a third of the time, I lose time and focus fiddling with the app and my watch instead of focusing on my workout.

It's a good workout app. It's easy to create workouts and I love the fact that you can organize them in folders. Would give five stars, but it is super glitchy with my Apple Watch. Seems to only work about half the time, I'll mark sets complete on my Watch and it won't sync to the phone and vice ver
Watch app needs better functionality. I should be able to follow along on watch and phone, not one or the other. Watch app doesn't show last weight and rep count. Hard to progress without.

observations.title: Carrying on from the same place after a pause
passages: At home a big screen helps you make out a movement without turning to the phone all the time. But after a short pause the cast can drop or start the program again from the beginning. Then even a session someone liked has to be reconstructed from memory, switching between the controls and the hunt for the right moment.

The viewing conditions and the connection method supported are worth finding out before the start. Then test stopping, resuming and coming back after switching away. A useful outcome is the same demonstration continuing from the chosen place, with the phone left as a convenient way to control the session.

A ring at the door or a brief switch to another app is a normal part of a home workout. A saved position in the video lets you come back without searching, and a separate completion mark keeps the paused time from counting as exercise. Here the quality of a small library with reliable playback can matter more than the size of the catalog.

quotes.text: Love this app but hate that it literally blocks you from screen mirroring to your tv :( I can't afford internet right now let alone a premium subscription so it just sucks that I have to do it off of my tiny phone screen
How are you gonna make me update the app and it still can't even chromecast properly? Make it make sense. Love the workouts, app is meh
When using IPhone or IPad to cast app program to tv, the program restarts from beginning, losing my place in workout EVERY time I pause my workout! This is so frustrating. Why does this happen?

observations.title: Bringing the video, the reps and the timer into line
passages: In a specialist’s home program the description of a movement can be clear while the demonstration and the timer diverge from the time prescribed. The person has to stop the video by hand in order to follow the parameters they were given. A prompt like that doesn’t accompany the work; it creates another source of inconsistency.

The prescribed reps, hold times and transitions have to be delivered separately, keeping their link to the program. What needs testing is whether the count displayed matches the specialist’s original settings. Convenient controls help someone follow those settings; they must not quietly replace them with other values.

A person should not have two instructions that contradict each other: hold the position for thirty seconds on the card, while in the video the next movement has already started. For a product with a specialist’s programs it helps to store the parameters separately from the clip and to show what changes have been made to a prescribed session.

And some exercises are the opposite. one is supposed to be 10 seconds for each rep and it will tell you a minute 30 for each rep. Makes no sense. My PT says th

I wish the app would actually time the exercises appropriately based on the speed and timing my PT has entered. The videos are going close to 5-10x the speed she actually wants be doing these exercises so I have to reach over and pause and restart and pause and restart.
Does a good job of describing the exercises but the time allocated to each is too long or too short. Too little time between exercises. Should be a way to adjust that.

sections.title: Saving what was done and coming back
sections.intro: The next session begins with the last one. The log and the chosen program have to survive pauses and a change of device.

observations.title: Not losing your place in the program
passages: After a migration the record can look complete while the totals change. In the review below the estimated records after an import are inflated relative to the original sessions. So what has to be checked is the exercises, the values and the rules of calculation, not a single count of workouts transferred.

Losing the log itself is even more obvious: the work that was done disappears. On an update and on a change of device it helps to keep access to the previous copy and to show what the restore contains. A person has to be able to open a familiar session and check it against the original.

The chosen program is a separate piece of data. A reset of difficulty or of content during an update should not be masked by the fact that the log is still available. Coming back starts from the last workout completed and a clear next step; days that have passed are not in themselves sessions that were done.

quotes.text: I imported my workouts and stats from the Strong app into Hevy, and all of my stats are inflated by at least 2 to 3 times more than what I actually did. This means that my 1RM and PRs are wrong. I can't accurately track my progress.
Dislike this last update and the changes made it less user friendly. And deleted all my work outs.. after 599 workouts logged time to find something else…

This is a good app, easy to use and has a lot of variety. However… every time there's an update, my training program resets! Activities are removed or added without notice. Difficulty settings are also reset. This inconsistency is really annoying.

art.alt: Illustration for the theme “Not losing your place in the program”.

observations.title: Supporting a return without extra noise
passages: A streak of marks, a small reward or a shared competition can give a pleasant reason to come back. For some people that is a value of its own alongside the program. Others, at that same moment, want nothing but the log and their previous exercises; a game screen should not complicate that path.

It helps to make the form of support selectable and to keep the history regardless of taking part. Coming back after a break, a person needs to see their earlier work and understand the next step. It is worth checking separately that changes to the visuals don’t get in the way of finding exercises and comparing one’s own records.

A person can be allowed to choose what they want to see after a session: a short summary, a personal record, or only the saved log. These are different forms of feedback. To test the idea it is more useful to learn whether the chosen summary helps someone come again than to count how many congratulation screens were opened.

quotes.text: The streak feature and ratings on how well you do truly stand out in this app, the free option includes all the necessities, highly recommend

There is such a wonderful variety of classes on here. I mostly do stretching and yoga and am always discovering new classes and trainers, so I don't think I will ever run out of options! I also really like the monthly step competitions as they motivate me to get in some extra walks.

conclusion.title: Test a whole session
conclusion.body:
The first priority is one session, from the start to a saved result. In the gym that means the previous values, a quick mark and the watch working; at home, a clear demonstration, a pause and a continuation. The reviews show how a failure in one small transition makes a person service the app instead of doing the program they chose. New collections will not fix that.

Then it is worth picking the main product: a log for training on your own, a creator-led course, or a trainer’s workspace. Each has its own reason to come back and to pay. They don’t have to be combined at launch. Whether the history survives and how accurately the conditions are described can be checked directly; a suitable load and the results of training cannot be deduced from a convenient interface or from a few positive reviews.
